# Fixtures whose recorded golden output no longer matches this binary.
#
# tools/diff/run has been in the tree unreferenced by the Makefile and by
# .github/workflows/ci.yml since it was written, so nothing ever ran it and
# nothing ever noticed the corpus drifting away from the goldens. Wiring it up
# meant starting from a run that already had findings. Each one is listed here
# so the harness can fail on the next one.
#
# Each line is `<fixture> <kind>`. The kind is checked: a line excuses one kind
# of finding against that fixture and nothing else, so a fixture listed as a
# golden mismatch that starts erroring, timing out, or losing its golden file
# fails the build. A path on its own is refused rather than read as a wildcard.
#
# The kind, and not the content of the difference, is what a line is keyed on,
# and that is measured rather than assumed. Building this same tree for
# GOARCH=amd64 and running it under Rosetta, nine of the twenty-nine fixtures
# that mismatch on both CPUs mismatch differently -- examples/gbm.tw's first
# difference is line 5 on arm64 and line 15 on amd64 -- so keying a line on the
# content would make this file per-CPU. The suite allow-list has no such problem
# and is keyed on the divergence itself.
#
# The list may only shrink: the way to remove a line is to re-record that
# fixture's golden deliberately, in a commit that says what changed and why the
# new output is right.
#
# Recording the goldens again wholesale was the alternative and is worse. The
# stale output is evidence of what the language used to do, and four of the five
# groups below are behaviour changes nobody wrote down. Overwriting them would
# destroy the only record that they happened.
#
# Measured with `make diff` on the branch this file arrived on, an arm64 Darwin
# build of go1.27: 354 fixtures, 321 verified, 33 golden mismatches, no missing
# goldens and no errors. The same run at 209ed56, the last commit that
# re-recorded any golden, gives 21, so 12 of these were introduced after the
# last refreeze and 21 were already stale when it happened.

# --- 1. The standard library grew ------------------------------------------
# These fixtures print a module record, so every function added to std/nn.tw,
# std/num.tw or std/shapes.tw changes their output: rope, rms_norm, swiglu,
# geglu, glu, attention_causal_rope, all, any, count_nonzero and the rest. Not
# a behaviour change; the fixtures are just a census of the library.
testdata/cases/checker_record_66eeab0c8344d05b.tw    golden-mismatch
testdata/cases/interp_import_1022264b14f2a00f.tw     golden-mismatch
testdata/cases/interp_import_37899042553abb30.tw     golden-mismatch
testdata/cases/interp_import_4a58879b83eb92d6.tw     golden-mismatch
testdata/cases/interp_import_4d2712abe7c4b462.tw     golden-mismatch
testdata/cases/interp_import_7a6fc56871a75287.tw     golden-mismatch
testdata/cases/interp_import_b841ee1f876aabe5.tw     golden-mismatch
testdata/cases/interp_serialize_e30bc4f3260b7f3b.tw  golden-mismatch
testdata/examples/classifier.tw                      golden-mismatch
testdata/examples/nn_xor.tw                          golden-mismatch
testdata/std/nn.tw                                   golden-mismatch
testdata/std/num.tw                                  golden-mismatch
testdata/std/shapes.tw                               golden-mismatch

# --- 2. The language was renamed -------------------------------------------
# The golden still says `unknown name "martin"` where the binary now says
# `unknown name "twill"`. Stale since 1c3b094, the Raster to Twill rename.
testdata/cases/interp_bench_ed770eb055f5570a.tw      golden-mismatch
testdata/cases/interp_cumulative_229df79f2eb3b279.tw golden-mismatch
testdata/cases/interp_cumulative_a85534954edf5f98.tw golden-mismatch
testdata/cases/interp_examples_3cc12389cbdde183.tw   golden-mismatch
testdata/cases/interp_examples_6e2eb52ac486631f.tw   golden-mismatch
testdata/cases/interp_format_run_69ac71c64b0eee40.tw golden-mismatch

# --- 3. Two errors moved from run time to check time ------------------------
# The checker now catches what the interpreter used to, so the message changed
# class as well as wording. Both are improvements and neither was recorded.
#   axis 5 out of range for rank 2
#     -> shape error: axis out of range for [1, 2]: it has 2 axes, numbered 0 to 1
#   cannot compare these values with "<"
#     -> shape error: cannot order a list with "<": ordering is numbers and strings
testdata/cases/interp_cumulative_d2e59cce3c8e2e96.tw golden-mismatch
testdata/cases/interp_equality_bf072a1e7bc0c7c6.tw   golden-mismatch

# --- 4. Floating point results moved ----------------------------------------
# The canonical dump prints every float as a hex literal, so these are exact
# last-bit changes in a forward value, not formatting. All ten still mismatch on
# an amd64 build of this same tree, so they are changes in twill and not in the
# CPU; two of them, examples/montecarlo_option.tw and the finance case, need a
# budget above the two-minute default to show it under emulation. Nobody knows
# which commit moved them, because nothing was watching.
#   examples/gbm.tw         test regression RMSE 0.65947  -> 0.660285
#   examples/signal_opt.tw  step 200 Sharpe    4.655568   -> 4.655621
testdata/cases/interp_finance_90d36d289f85c057.tw    golden-mismatch
testdata/examples/attention.tw                       golden-mismatch
testdata/examples/backtest.tw                        golden-mismatch
testdata/examples/cnn.tw                             golden-mismatch
testdata/examples/gbm.tw                             golden-mismatch
testdata/examples/minibatch.tw                       golden-mismatch
testdata/examples/mlp.tw                             golden-mismatch
testdata/examples/montecarlo_option.tw               golden-mismatch
testdata/examples/records.tw                         golden-mismatch
testdata/examples/signal_opt.tw                      golden-mismatch

# --- 5. Architecture-dependent floats ---------------------------------------
# These two agree on an amd64 build of this tree and differ on arm64, so the
# goldens were recorded on amd64 and these fixtures are not portable. They will
# show up as "agrees here; delete its line" on an amd64 CI runner, which is why
# a cleared allow-list entry is a note and not a failure.
testdata/cases/interp_bench_bca6ee0bb6f0f500.tw      golden-mismatch
testdata/examples/linreg.tw                          golden-mismatch
